title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ الددو يشارك في مؤتمر دولي بقطر
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Takes Part in an International Conference in Qatar
body_ar: يشارك سماحة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو-حفظه الله- رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء بموريتانيا على مدار ثلاثة أيام ابتداء من يوم الجمعة 08 رجب 1437ھـ الموافق 15 إبريل 2016م بالعاصمة القطرية الدوحة في "المؤتمر العالمي للتعليم الشرعي وسبل ترقيته" المنظم من طرف الاتحاد العالمي لعلماء المسلمين برعاية من حكومة دولة قطر، ويشارك في هذا المؤتمر إلى جانب الشيخ كوكبة من العلماء ورؤساء مؤسسات التعليم الشرعي والباحثين في مجال الشريعة من بلدان مختلفة.
body_en: His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew (may God preserve him), president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars in Mauritania, is taking part over three days, beginning on Friday 8 Rajab 1437 AH, corresponding to 15 April 2016, in the Qatari capital Doha, in the 'International Conference on Sharia Education and the Means of Advancing It', organised by the International Union of Muslim Scholars under the patronage of the government of the State of Qatar. Taking part in this conference alongside the Sheikh is a distinguished company of scholars, heads of institutions of Sharia education, and researchers in the field of the Sharia from various countries.

flags.context: المؤتمر العالمي للتعليم الشرعي وسبل ترقيته
flags.note: 'التعليم الشرعي' is the whole curriculum of the revealed sciences as taught in traditional institutions, wider than fiqh alone. 'Sharia education' is short and is the phrase these institutions use of themselves in English, but it can mislead an English reader into thinking of law schools. Worth fixing once for the corpus.

translator_notes: سماحة is a higher honorific than فضيلة, which the same site uses of the Sheikh elsewhere; English has no matching pair, so both are rendered 'His Eminence' and the difference is noted here rather than invented in the English.
مركز تكوين العلماء is rendered 'the Centre for the Formation of Scholars', the institution's own usage; تكوين here is formation or training, not creation.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date, not the date of composition.
